title: Diagnosing and recording root caries: A survey among international dentists
summary:
Background:
As life expectancy increases, more people keep their natural teeth into old age. As a result, a type of tooth decay called root caries is becoming more common among older adults. Root caries develops on the root surfaces of teeth, which may become exposed due to gum recession. In addition, age-related limitations in oral hygiene or general health problems can increase the risk. Because root caries is becoming more common, especially in older populations, it is important to better understand how dentists diagnose, document, and treat this condition.

Objective:
The aim of this study is to investigate how dentists around the world manage root caries. The study will assess dentists’ knowledge, attitudes, as well as their diagnostic and treatment approaches.

Methods:
This study will be conducted as an international cross-sectional online survey using a standardized and validated questionnaire. Licensed dentists from approximately 40 countries will be invited to participate through an international network of dental professional societies.

interventions.name:
The planned study is an international cross-sectional study without a control group. The study aims to assess the attitudes, knowledge, and practices of dentists on the subject of root caries using a standardized questionnaire.
